title: Keep NC Working Act
lastAction: Ref to the Com on Commerce and Economic Development, if favorable, Appropriations, if favorable, Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill establishes a Short-Time Compensation Program that allows employers to reduce employee work hours by 10-60% as an alternative to layoffs, with affected employees receiving partial unemployment benefits to offset lost wages. The program requires employer applications, Division approval, maintenance of employee health and retirement benefits, and is capped at 52 weeks per employee, with $100,000 appropriated for implementation.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this program helps businesses avoid permanent layoffs during economic downturns by spreading work reductions across multiple employees rather than eliminating jobs entirely. Employees keep their jobs, health insurance, and retirement benefits while receiving partial unemployment compensation, maintaining income stability and preserving the employer-employee relationship when business temporarily declines.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue the program could be misused by employers to reduce labor costs without genuine economic hardship, that it complicates unemployment insurance administration and costs, and that partial benefits might not adequately replace lost wages for participating workers. Some may also question whether employers will actually use this instead of layoffs, or whether it primarily benefits larger employers with resources to navigate the approval process.
